title: The Ramparts of Ice
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Koyuki Hikawa, called the 'Ice Queen' for keeping everyone at a distance after boys teased her height in middle school, is drawn out by overly friendly Minato, his kind friend Yota and her childhood friend Miki. The full-color webtoon follows the four through misunderstandings, rejected and returned confessions, and Minato's struggle with loneliness and self-hatred, ending with two couples (Wikipedia; MangaPlaza blurb via AniList and MU).
life_message: Opening up to others, being honest about feelings and helping friends face their fears leads to real connection.

content.note: Emotional drama only (MU Emotional Roller Coaster).
Teen romance and confessions; Minato's past dating seen as insincere (Wikipedia); MangaDex safe.
Past teasing, social anxiety, Momoka's emotional abuse, Minato's self-hatred and fear of loneliness (Wikipedia; MU Introvert/s, Emotional Roller Coaster).
Dating someone to get over another, shown as harmful (Wikipedia).

dominant: Friendship and emotional honesty; overcoming fear of others; healthy relationships

frames.aligns: Friends draw a wounded girl out; Minato learns to stop using others (Wikipedia).
Humility and repentance in Minato's change.
Healing from past hurt through community.
Putting the best construction on others; misunderstandings resolved.
Small-group accountability: four friends helping each other grow.
Names emotional abuse and honors mental health.
Right speech and compassion heal misunderstandings.
Emotional abuse recognized; anti-bullying; consent-minded relationships.
Fear overcome by love and changed thought.
Worth of each person; healing through community.
Truthful living and service to friends.
Guarding speech; mocking Koyuki's height shown as harmful.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Koyuki confronts Minato with words; hurts resolved by talking (Wikipedia).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Students choose their own friendships and romances (Wikipedia).

Civic vs kin.evidence: Friend group, not family, is the support (MU Friendship).

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Popular and loner students become equals (blurb).

folkways.japan: School 'loud groups', the class-idol label Miki dislikes and the pressure to keep a pleasing image reflect Japanese school social hierarchies and group harmony.

delivery.evidence: Themes carried by character arcs per Wikipedia; no review on delivery opened (to verify).
delivery.note: Unhealthy patterns appear in characters, including Minato himself, who changes rather than being simply condemned.

winners_losers: Koyuki and Minato, Miki and Yota end as couples; Momoka's relationship with Minato ends. Sympathy goes to honesty and patience.
